messages.text: Voltage Protection is showing and it won't mine.  Just got this unit today
Searched the web · Bitaxe Gamma AxeOS "voltage protection" error
Searched the web · ESP-Miner bitaxe "voltage" protection screen power fault inp

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let's get your new miner hashing.

I couldn't find the exact wording "Voltage Protection" in the Bitaxe firmware docs. So I won't guess what that message means yet. The closest message I found in the official Bitaxe firmware (ESP-Miner on GitHub) is 
"Power Fault Detected. Check your Power Supply."
 That one comes from the power supply side, so the power supply is the first thing to check:

1. Is the miner plugged into the power brick that came in the box, using the round barrel plug? A Bitaxe needs 
5V DC Only! Anything else will damage the Bitaxe.
 A USB-C cable alone won't run it.
2. If you used a different power supply, unplug it and don't use it again until we've checked its label. Too much voltage is a known cause: 
The Bitaxe max input voltage is 5.5V.


Can you reply with:
- Which miner this is (the Bitaxe Gamma 602?)
- Which power supply you're using, and what its label says for output (for example "5V 6A")

If you can, also send a photo of the screen showing the message. That lets me see the exact wording and any numbers next to it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened your photo. Here's what the screen shows:

- A red **VOLTAGE PROTECTION** box with the code **Guru Meditation #····**
- BM1370 chip, 0.0 GH/s, 33 °C and only **0.062 W** of power draw. That means the miner has switched power off to the hashing chip, so it isn't mining at all.
- Wi-Fi is connected at **192.168.4.68**. That's good, because it means we can read more details from the miner's web page.

About the code: "Guru Meditation" codes come from the NerdQaxe firmware family. For example, a NerdQaxe++ owner reported 
"PSU error - Guru Meditation #····"
 on the firmware's GitHub page. I couldn't find a public explanation of **#····** specifically, so I won't guess at its exact meaning. The words "Voltage Protection" plus the chip being switched off do point at the power supply as the first thing to rule out.

Two quick checks:

1. **Power supply:** is it the one that came in the box? What does its label say for output (for example "5V 6A" or "12V 10A")?
2. **Web page:** on a phone or computer on the same Wi-Fi, open **http://192.168.4.68**. Send me a screenshot of the dashboard showing the input voltage and the firmware version.

If the power plug or brick feels hot, or you smell anything burning, unplug it right away and tell me.
Heres what its showing and its not mining or barely

Your new screenshot didn't come through on my side. The only image I have is the first photo of the miner's screen. Could you try attaching it again?

While you do, please also tell me:

1. **Which power supply** you're using: is it the one from the box, and what does its label say for output (for example "5V 6A")? This matters most, because "Voltage Protection" points at power first.
2. **What the web page at http://192.168.4.68 shows** for input voltage, hashrate and firmware version. If the screenshot won't attach, typing those three numbers works just as well.

"Barely mining" plus the voltage warning usually means the miner is cutting power to the chip. These two answers will tell us whether the cause is the power supply or the board.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, I opened the screenshot. Before anything else, I need to correct something I said earlier.

**This isn't a Bitaxe Gamma.** The dashboard expects 4,896 GH/s from BM1370 chips and shows a 12.1 V input. That matches a **NerdQaxe++**, which runs on 12V. My earlier "5V only" note was for the Bitaxe. Please don't connect a 5V supply to this unit.

What the dashboard shows:
- **Current Voltage 12.1 V:** power is reaching the board at the right level.
- **ASIC Voltage 0.00 V, 0.00 A, 0.1 W:** the board's voltage regulator has switched the hashing chips off. That's what the "Voltage Protection" warning means here.
- **0 shares since connect.** The all-time best difficulty of 979 M suggests the unit did hash at some point.

So power is getting in, but the miner shuts the chips off when it tries to start them. Most often that happens because the power supply can't deliver enough current under load, or because of a regulator fault. Let's rule out the easy one:

1. **Cold restart:** unplug the 12V power cable from the miner, wait 30 seconds, plug it back in, and watch the dashboard for about 2 minutes. Does ASIC Voltage come up above 0 V and does the hashrate climb?
2. **Power supply label:** is this the brick that came in the box? What does it say for output (for example "12V 10A")?
3. **Firmware version:** you'll find it on the System or Settings page of the same web page.

Send me those three and we'll take the next step.
Did 1 already, Yes its the brick that came with it more like a metal box. 12V 29A.  3 latest firmware updated to 1.1.2
Read github.com/shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus/releases

Thanks, that rules out a lot:

- **Power supply:** a 12V 29A supply is about 350W. That's plenty for this miner, and the dashboard shows a clean 12.1 V coming in. Supply cap····'t the problem.
- **Firmware:** on the official NerdQaxe firmware GitHub, the newest release page I could load still lists v1.1.0 as the latest. Your 1.1.2 is at least as new as anything I can see, so it's fine. No need to roll back.
- **Restart:** done, with no change.

So the board gets good 12V in, but the regulator keeps 0 V on the chips. The miner's own log will say why it trips. That's the next check:

1. Open **http://192.168.4.68** and find the **Logs** page (in the menu, sometimes under System).
2. Restart the miner from the web page, and let the log run for about a minute after it boots.
3. Send me a screenshot or copy of the lines around the moment it trips. Look for words like **"voltage", "VR", "TPS", "PGOOD", "fault"** or **"Guru"**.

While it boots, two quick physical checks:
- Is the 12V plug pushed fully into the miner and screwed down or seated firmly (not loose or wobbly)?
- Do the fans spin up at power on?

If you notice any burning smell, or the plug or board feels very hot, unplug it straight away and tell me.

Its seated firmly-ish not like my Hammer miner where it click in, but its in there.  I lost my sense of smell with Covid so can't help you there, it could be on fire for all I know.  Its cold to the touch.

Hal here, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Thanks, that helps.

**Cold to the touch is expected here.** The chips are getting 0 V and the board draws about 0.1 W, so nothing on it is heating up. Since you can't rely on smell, use your eyes instead:

1. **Unplug the 12V cable** and look at both ends of the plug and the socket on the miner. Any browned, melted or blackened spots?
2. **Look over the board,** especially around the small square chips and coils near where the power comes in. Any scorch marks, bulging parts or anything that looks burnt?
3. **Reseat the plug** as firmly as it will go. A plug that's only "in there" can read a fine 12.1 V while idle, then sag when the miner switches the chips on. That sag alone can trip voltage protection. While it's booting, check that the fans spin up.

If you see any burn marks or melted plastic, leave it unplugged and tell me. Otherwise, after the reseat, send me:
- whether it starts hashing (ASIC voltage above 0 V), and
- if it still trips, the **Logs** page lines from the minute after boot. Look for "voltage", "VR", "TPS", "fault" or "Guru".

The log line is what will settle whether this is the plug or the board itself.
Sending screen shot once I find it.

Sounds good, take your time. If you can't spot it, the logs are usually in the web page's side menu, sometimes under "System" or a "Show logs" button. A photo of the screen works just as well as a screenshot.

Reading the regulator's status bits against the TPS53647 datasheet now.
Searched the web · TPS53647 datasheet STATUS_VOUT VOUT_OV_FAULT STATUS_WORD bit
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Handed to the team · Looks like a TPS53647 regulator fault (VOUT OV at enable). Done: cold power cycl

Your log shows what's going on. Here's what it says:

- **Input is fine:** `vin: 12.09`. Your power supply is delivering properly.
- **Fans are fine:** 3591 and 902 RPM.
- **The red line is the problem:** right after the miner sets the chips to 1.15 V, the voltage regulator (a TPS53647) reports **status word 8860, vout 80**. Read with the standard power-chip status codes (PMBus), that means the regulator saw an **output overvoltage fault**, switched itself off and flagged "power not good". That's the "Voltage Protection" on your screen, and it's why ASIC voltage stays at 0 V.

For comparison, another NerdQaxe++ owner posted this line from a regulator that was simply off: `TPS536X7_status bytes: 40, word: 0840, vout: 00`. Yours has the extra overvoltage-fault flag, so this isn't a power supply or Wi-Fi problem. It points at the regulator side of the board.

I've sent your log and every check we did to JD, our hardware lead. The team is offline now. They'll pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come to your email. For a faster route, join our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (JD). Post your log screenshot there.

Until then, please **leave the miner unplugged**.

One question helps JD a lot: **did this error appear straight out of the box, before you updated to 1.1.2**, or only after the update?
No other fault in the logs

Thanks, that helps. A single fault line, right at the moment the chips get powered, with nothing else going wrong, fits one specific trip by the voltage regulator. It doesn't look like a chain of software errors.

Everything we found is with JD, so nothing else is needed from the logs.

One thing still open: **did this error show up straight out of the box, before you updated to 1.1.2, or only after the update?** That tells JD whether the update is worth ruling out.

Keep it unplugged for now. The team picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET and will reply by email. If you post on the Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate), JD may get to it sooner.
